Important distinction

The Qur’an repeatedly says creation occurred in six ayyām, but it does not itself label an explicit “Day 1, Day 2 … Day 6” sequence like Genesis 1. Classical tafsīr sometimes maps the six to Sunday–Friday; interpretations of the length and nature of an yawm differ.

How lessons work

First session is diagnostic. We find out what is actually missing rather than assuming it is the current topic — most difficulties at A-Level trace back to something unresolved two years earlier.

Then a plan with dates on it. Topics sequenced against the exam timetable, with retrieval practice built in — testing yourself is the single best-evidenced study technique there is, and almost nobody uses it enough.

Past papers early, not last. Working under exam conditions from the start, marked against the real scheme, so the format stops being a variable by the time it matters.

Why Φ

A polyhistor is someone learned across many fields. The word has fallen out of use, which tells you something about how we decided to organise knowledge.

I have spent my working life crossing lines that were not supposed to be crossed. Materials science taught me how matter behaves; biomedical engineering taught me how it behaves when it is alive; neuroscience research asked how it behaves when it is thinking. None of those questions announced where one subject ended and the next began.

The same is true outside the lab. The questions that matter most — what exists, why, and what we owe each other — do not respect a syllabus. A student curious about the origin of the universe is asking a physics question, a philosophy question, and a theological one in the same breath. Telling them to pick a lane does not make them a better thinker. It makes them a narrower one.

Φ, the golden ratio, is the symbol because it keeps turning up where it has no business being — in shells and sunflower heads, in the Parthenon, in a sequence Fibonacci wrote down while counting rabbits. One proportion, surfacing across mathematics, biology, art and architecture, entirely indifferent to the boundaries we drew afterwards.

That is the whole idea of this place. Put the disciplines beside each other, let each speak in its own voice, and stay honest about where they agree, where they simply answer different questions, and where they genuinely conflict.

Before Adam

13.8 Billion Years of Cosmic, Geological, and Human History — Read Alongside Qur'an, Hadith, and Bible

Integrated Deep Time Study

Before Adam: The History of the Universe, Life, and Humanity

"We shall show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth." — Qur'an 41:53

This is a single story told twice. Modern cosmology, geology, and biology reconstruct what happened, in what order, and by what mechanism. The Qur'an, the Hadith, and the Bible speak to who is behind it, why it matters, and what it asks of us. Read in parallel — not in competition — the two accounts illuminate different faces of the same history.

How to read this page

Each epoch below is presented twice, side by side. The left panel is the scientific reconstruction: dated, measurable, revisable. The right panel gathers the scriptural material — Qur'anic verses, prophetic Hadith with their collection references, and Biblical passages (King James Version) — that religious tradition has brought to bear on the same moment.

Beneath each pair, a short synthesis notes where the two genuinely converge, where they simply address different questions, and where the correspondence has been overstated. Scripture is not a physics textbook, and this page does not treat it as one.

Jump to an epoch 0 · Before Time 1 · The Beginning 2 · First Light 3 · Stars & Elements 4 · Earth Forms 5 · First Life 6 · One Cell to Many 7 · The Creatures 8 · Extinctions 9 · Before Adam's Kind 10 · The Mind Awakes 11 · Adam Created 12 · Angels & Iblis 13 · The Trust The Six Days Two Accounts Scholars Differ Full Timeline

Before Time: The Eternal and the Unmeasured

t < 0 · outside physics, outside history

Before there was a "before" — the one question science cannot date and scripture answers without hesitation.

What science describes

General relativity breaks down at the first instant. Asking what came "before" the Big Bang may be malformed if time itself began there — like asking what lies north of the North Pole. Physics offers candidate frameworks, none confirmed:

  • Quantum cosmology — the universe as a quantum event with no classical prior state (Hartle–Hawking).
  • Eternal inflation — our cosmos a bubble in an endlessly inflating substrate.
  • Cyclic models — bounces rather than a single origin.

Each is mathematically serious and observationally out of reach. Science's honest position here is agnosticism: our equations run out before the question does.

What scripture says
Qur'an

"He is the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden."

Surah al-Hadid 57:3
Qur'an

"Originator (Badīʿ) of the heavens and the earth."

Surah al-Anʿam 6:101 — origination without precedent or template
Hadith

"There was Allah, and there was nothing before Him; and His Throne was upon the water."

Sahih al-Bukhari 3191, Kitab Bad' al-Khalq
Hadith

"Allah decreed the measures of creation fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth."

Sahih Muslim 2653
Bible

"Before the mountains were brought forth… from everlasting to everlasting, thou art God."

Psalm 90:2 (KJV)
Bible

"In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God."

John 1:1 (KJV)
Reading them together: This is the cleanest example of the two accounts asking different questions. Physics asks what the initial conditions were and finds its own tools failing at the boundary. Scripture does not supply initial conditions; it asserts an eternal, uncaused Reality that is not itself an item within the universe. Al-Ghazālī's argument in the Tahāfut — that whatever begins to exist requires a cause — was formulated centuries before cosmology found a beginning to date, and it neither depends on nor is confirmed by that finding.

The Beginning: Space, Time, and the First Matter

13.8 billion years ago · t = 0 to 3 minutes

Everything that exists emerges from a state hotter and denser than any we can reproduce — and immediately begins to expand.

What science describes

Not an explosion into space, but the emergence of space-time itself. The sequence is tightly constrained by particle physics and confirmed by observation:

  • 10⁻³⁶ s — inflation: the universe expands by a factor of ~10²⁶, smoothing and flattening it.
  • 10⁻⁶ s — quarks bind into protons and neutrons.
  • 3 min — Big Bang nucleosynthesis forges hydrogen, deuterium, helium-3, helium-4, and trace lithium in ratios we still measure today.

The primary evidence is redshift: light from distant galaxies is stretched in proportion to distance (Hubble, 1929). Space is expanding, and rewinding that expansion converges on a single dense origin. The measured helium abundance (~24% by mass) matches nucleosynthesis predictions with striking precision.

What scripture says
Qur'an

أَوَلَمْ يَرَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَنَّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ كَانَتَا رَتْقًا فَفَتَقْنَاهُمَا

"…the heavens and the earth were a joined entity (ratq), and We separated them (fataqnāhumā)…"

Surah al-Anbiya 21:30
Qur'an

"…then He directed Himself to the heaven while it was smoke (dukhān)."

Surah Fussilat 41:11
Qur'an

"And the heaven We constructed with strength, and indeed, We are [its] expander (mūsiʿūn)."

Surah adh-Dhariyat 51:47
Qur'an

"When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, 'Be,' and it is."

Surah al-Baqarah 2:117 — creation by command, not by struggle
Bible

"In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth."

Genesis 1:1 (KJV)
Bible

"…the things which are seen were not made of things which do appear."

Hebrews 11:3 (KJV)
Bible

"…that stretcheth out the heavens as a curtain, and spreadeth them out as a tent."

Isaiah 40:22 (KJV)
Reading them together: Three scriptural themes line up with the cosmological picture in broad shape — an absolute beginning, an early undifferentiated state, and an expanding heaven. Both traditions also reject the idea that the universe is self-explanatory: Hebrews' "not made of things which do appear" and the Qur'anic Badīʿ both point to origination rather than rearrangement.
An honest caveat. The concordist reading of 21:30, 41:11, and 51:47 as "the Qur'an predicted the Big Bang" is popular but contested. Classical exegetes (al-Ṭabarī, al-Qurṭubī, Ibn Kathīr) read ratq/fatq as the heaven withholding rain and the earth withholding vegetation, then both being opened — an agricultural image, not a cosmological one. Mūsiʿūn was widely read as "possessing vast power" or "the one who gives amply." These readings long predate modern cosmology. The point is not that the modern reading is illegitimate, but that it is a reading, arrived at after the science was known — which is a weaker kind of claim than prediction.

First Light: The Universe Becomes Transparent

380,000 years after the beginning

For nearly 400,000 years the cosmos is an opaque fog. Then it clears, and light travels free for the first time.

What science describes

Until recombination, free electrons scatter every photon almost immediately — the universe glows but is opaque, like the inside of a cloud. As expansion cools the plasma below roughly 3,000 K, electrons finally bind to nuclei to form neutral atoms. Photons decouple and stream outward unimpeded.

That light is still arriving. Stretched by 13.8 billion years of expansion into microwaves, it is the Cosmic Microwave Background — discovered accidentally by Penzias and Wilson in 1965, and mapped in exquisite detail by COBE, WMAP, and Planck. Its temperature fluctuations, one part in 100,000, are the seeds of every galaxy that would later form.

What scripture says
Bible

"And God said, Let there be light: and there was light."

Genesis 1:3 (KJV)
Bible

"And the earth was without form, and void; and darkness was upon the face of the deep."

Genesis 1:2 (KJV)
Qur'an

"[All] praise is due to Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and made the darkness and the light."

Surah al-Anʿam 6:1
Qur'an

"Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth."

Surah an-Nur 24:35 — the Verse of Light
Hadith

"The angels were created from light, the jinn from a smokeless flame of fire, and Adam from what has been described to you."

Sahih Muslim 2996
Reading them together: Both scriptures place light near the start of creation and before the sun — a sequence that once looked like a scientific error in Genesis (light on day one, sun on day four) but sits comfortably with cosmology, where the universe is bathed in radiation for hundreds of millions of years before the first star ignites. What scripture is chiefly doing here, however, is theological: light functions throughout both traditions as the primary metaphor for knowledge, guidance, and divine presence. The Verse of Light is a meditation on how God is known, not on photon decoupling.

Stars and the Forging of the Elements

13.4 billion – 4.6 billion years ago

Gravity gathers hydrogen into furnaces. Inside them, every element heavier than helium is manufactured — including the atoms now in your body.

What science describes

Density fluctuations in the primordial gas collapse under gravity. The first stars ignite roughly 100–200 million years in — enormous, short-lived, and made purely of hydrogen and helium. Within them, nuclear fusion builds heavier nuclei step by step: hydrogen to helium, then carbon, oxygen, neon, silicon, up to iron.

Iron is the terminus — fusing it consumes rather than releases energy. The core collapses, and the star explodes. In that supernova, and in neutron-star mergers, the heaviest elements form and are scattered into interstellar space, seeding the next generation of stars and planets.

The consequence: the calcium in your bones, the oxygen you breathe, the iron in your blood were manufactured inside stars that died before the Sun existed. This is not poetry; it is stellar nucleosynthesis, worked out by Burbidge, Burbidge, Fowler and Hoyle in 1957.

What scripture says
Qur'an

"And We have certainly beautified the nearest heaven with lamps."

Surah al-Mulk 67:5; cf. as-Saffat 37:6
Qur'an

"Blessed is He who placed in the sky great stars and placed therein a [burning] lamp and a luminous moon."

Surah al-Furqan 25:61
Qur'an

"The sun and the moon [move] by precise calculation (ḥusbān)."

Surah ar-Rahman 55:5
Qur'an

"And We sent down iron, wherein is great military might and benefits for the people."

Surah al-Hadid 57:25 — "sent down" (anzalnā)
Bible

"He telleth the number of the stars; he calleth them all by their names."

Psalm 147:4 (KJV)
Bible

"Lift up your eyes on high, and behold who hath created these things."

Isaiah 40:26 (KJV)
Bible

"…when the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy."

Job 38:7 (KJV)
Reading them together: Both scriptures treat the stars as ordered and numbered rather than random — a conviction that underwrote centuries of Islamic and Christian astronomy. Al-Battānī, al-Ṭūsī, and Ibn al-Shāṭir catalogued and modelled the heavens precisely because they took ḥusbān, "precise calculation," as a description of reality worth measuring. Copernicus's lunar model reproduces Ibn al-Shāṭir's almost exactly.
On 57:25 and iron. The verse's anzalnā ("we sent down") is frequently cited as a reference to iron's extraterrestrial origin in supernovae. But the Qur'an uses the same verb for rain, for scripture, for garments (7:26) and for cattle (39:6) — where the sense is clearly one of divine bestowal rather than physical descent. The astrophysical reading is available, but it is not the plain sense, and the verse's own context is about iron's usefulness to human society.

Earth Takes Shape

4.6 – 4.0 billion years ago

A collapsing cloud becomes a star with a disk of debris; the debris becomes worlds; one of them is placed where water can stay liquid.

What science describes

A molecular cloud, likely nudged by a nearby supernova shockwave, collapses and flattens into a spinning protoplanetary disk. The Sun ignites at the centre. Dust grains stick, then accrete into planetesimals, then planets.

  • 4.51 bya — a Mars-sized body strikes proto-Earth; the debris forms the Moon, which will stabilise Earth's axial tilt for billions of years.
  • 4.4 bya — the crust solidifies; the oldest known zircon crystals date from here.
  • 4.0 bya — oceans condense; plate tectonics begin recycling crust.

Earth sits in the habitable zone — close enough for liquid water, far enough to avoid Venus's runaway greenhouse. Its magnetic field, generated by a molten iron core, deflects the solar wind. Its atmosphere blocks lethal ultraviolet. Mountain roots extend deep into the crust, isostatically balancing the ranges above.

What scripture says
Qur'an

"And after that He spread the earth (daḥāhā). He extracted from it its water and its pasture."

Surah an-Naziʿat 79:30–31
Qur'an

"Have We not made the earth a resting place, and the mountains as stakes (awtād)?"

Surah an-Naba 78:6–7
Qur'an

"And We placed within the earth firmly set mountains, lest it should shift with them."

Surah al-Anbiya 21:31
Qur'an

"And We made the sky a protected ceiling (saqfan maḥfūẓan)."

Surah al-Anbiya 21:32
Qur'an

"And the heaven He raised and imposed the balance (mīzān)."

Surah ar-Rahman 55:7; cf. al-Hijr 15:19 "in due balance" (mawzūn)
Bible

"Let the waters under the heaven be gathered together unto one place, and let the dry land appear."

Genesis 1:9 (KJV)
Bible

"Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth?"

Job 38:4 (KJV)
Bible

"…he created it not in vain, he formed it to be inhabited."

Isaiah 45:18 (KJV)
Reading them together: The scriptural emphasis here is on calibration — mīzān, balance; mawzūn, in due measure; a world "formed to be inhabited." Modern astrophysics describes the same narrowness in different vocabulary: an orbit in the habitable band, a stabilising Moon, a shielding magnetosphere, a self-regulating carbon cycle. Whether that narrowness demands a designer or is a selection effect (we could only have arisen on a planet that permitted us) is a live philosophical dispute, not a settled scientific result.
On the six days. Both traditions describe creation in six stages (Qur'an 7:54, 41:9–12; Genesis 1). Qur'an 41:9–12 gives a breakdown often read as two periods for the earth, four for its provisions, two for the heavens — apparently eight, which classical exegetes resolved by treating the four as inclusive of the first two. The Arabic yawm and Hebrew yom both admit of "period" as well as "day," and the Qur'an itself uses a day of a thousand years (22:47) and of fifty thousand (70:4). 2 Peter 3:8 makes the same move: "one day is with the Lord as a thousand years." Whether that licenses geological ages, or is a category error imposed on a liturgical text, divides scholars in both faiths.

Water and the First Life

4.0 – 3.5 billion years ago

In water, chemistry crosses a threshold and begins to copy itself. Everything alive descends from that event.

What science describes

Earth's early oceans, hydrothermal vents, and possibly tidal pools host a rich prebiotic chemistry. Amino acids, nucleotides, and lipids form readily under plausible early conditions — Miller and Urey demonstrated this in 1953, and meteorites carry amino acids ready-made.

The leading model is an RNA world: RNA can both store information and catalyse reactions, solving the chicken-and-egg problem of which came first, genes or enzymes. Lipid membranes spontaneously form vesicles, enclosing the chemistry into proto-cells.

By 3.5 billion years ago, stromatolites — layered mats built by microbial colonies — appear in the rock record in Western Australia. All extant life traces to a single common ancestor, LUCA, sharing one genetic code, one chirality, one core metabolism. Life on Earth began once, and everything since is descent with modification.

What scripture says
Qur'an

وَجَعَلْنَا مِنَ الْمَاءِ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ حَيٍّ

"…and We made from water every living thing. Then will they not believe?"

Surah al-Anbiya 21:30
Qur'an

"And it is He who has created from water a human being."

Surah al-Furqan 25:54
Qur'an

"…and He sends down rain from the sky, and We produce thereby pairs of various plants."

Surah Ta-Ha 20:53
Bible

"Let the waters bring forth abundantly the moving creature that hath life."

Genesis 1:20 (KJV)
Bible

"…and the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters."

Genesis 1:2 (KJV)
Bible

"Let the earth bring forth grass, the herb yielding seed."

Genesis 1:11 (KJV)
Reading them together: This is the closest and least strained convergence on the page. Both scriptures make water the medium of life, and Genesis has life emerging from the waters and the land rather than being assembled from nothing — "let the waters bring forth," "let the earth bring forth." Modern biology says exactly this: life is aqueous chemistry, and every cell is still mostly water. Notably, the Qur'anic statement is unqualified and universal — every living thing — which is a stronger and more falsifiable claim than the surrounding culture's cosmologies made.

From One Cell to Many: The Long Apprenticeship

2.4 billion – 541 million years ago

Microbes poison the air with oxygen, then learn to live on it, then learn to live together. Three billion years of the story happen at a scale no eye could see.

What science describes

2.4 bya — The Great Oxidation Event. Cyanobacteria evolve oxygenic photosynthesis. Oxygen, a waste product, first rusts the dissolved iron out of the oceans — laying down the banded iron formations we now mine — then floods the atmosphere. It is the largest pollution catastrophe in Earth's history and lethal to the anaerobes that then ruled the planet. It also builds the ozone layer that will later make dry land survivable.

1.8 bya — The eukaryotic cell. One cell engulfs another and, instead of digesting it, keeps it. The captive becomes the mitochondrion. Aerobic respiration extracts roughly sixteen times more energy per glucose molecule than fermentation, and that energy budget is what makes large, complex cells affordable. Mitochondria still carry their own separate DNA — the fingerprint of a merger that never fully dissolved.

1.2 – 1.0 bya — The first true multicellularity. Bangiomorpha pubescens, a fossil red alga from Arctic Canada, is the earliest known organism with differentiated cell types and sexual reproduction. Cells stop merely sticking together and begin specialising.

The transition required three genuine inventions:

  • Adhesion — cadherins and integrins, molecular velcro that makes cells hold rank.
  • Communication — signalling pathways so a cell can act on information from its neighbours rather than only from its own surroundings.
  • Programmed death — apoptosis. A cell must be able to die on cue for the body to take shape. Individual survival is subordinated to the whole.

800 – 635 mya. Choanoflagellates, the closest living relatives of animals, show the intermediate stage: single cells that form colonies when conditions call for it. Volvox algae do the same today — a living demonstration of the threshold being crossed. Then the Cryogenian glaciations ("Snowball Earth") nearly sterilise the planet, and the Ediacaran biota that follows produces the first large, soft-bodied, visibly complex organisms.

Complex multicellularity evolved independently at least six times — in animals, land plants, red algae, brown algae, and twice in fungi. It is a solution the living world reached for repeatedly.

What scripture says
Qur'an

قُلْ سِيرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَانظُرُوا كَيْفَ بَدَأَ الْخَلْقَ

"Say: Travel through the earth and observe how He began creation."

Surah al-ʿAnkabut 29:20 — an instruction to investigate origins in the ground itself
Qur'an

"What is wrong with you that you do not attribute to Allah due grandeur, while He has created you in stages (aṭwāran)?"

Surah Nuh 71:13–14
Qur'an

"…and you see the earth barren, but when We send down rain upon it, it quivers and swells and grows every kind of beautiful pair."

Surah al-Hajj 22:5 — life latent in the lifeless
Qur'an

"…and He dispersed throughout it from every creature."

Surah Luqman 31:10
Qur'an

"Exalted is He who created all pairs — from what the earth grows, and from themselves, and from that which they do not know."

Surah Ya-Sin 36:36 — pairing extended to what was then unknown
Bible

"Let the earth bring forth grass, the herb yielding seed… whose seed is in itself."

Genesis 1:11 (KJV)
Bible

"…thou sendest forth thy spirit, they are created: and thou renewest the face of the earth."

Psalm 104:30 (KJV)
Bible

"…so is this great and wide sea, wherein are things creeping innumerable, both small and great beasts."

Psalm 104:25 (KJV)
Reading them together: Qur'an 29:20 is the most methodologically striking verse on this page: it does not assert a mechanism, it issues an instruction — go into the earth and look at how creation started. That is, in effect, a mandate for palaeontology. The verse's classical readings vary, but on any reading it treats the physical record of beginnings as something a believer is told to examine rather than avoid. And 36:36's "pairs… from that which they do not know" was, to its first audience, an open category — the sexual reproduction that Bangiomorpha records is exactly the sort of thing that category later came to hold.
What scripture does not do here. Three billion years of microbial and single-celled history have no scriptural narrative at all — no verse describes mitochondria, cell adhesion, or the Ediacaran. Neither book claims to be exhaustive about the other's subject. The silence is not an omission; it reflects that these texts address meaning, accountability, and relationship with God, not cell biology.

The Great Diversification: Bellies, Two Legs, and Four

541 – 66 million years ago

Animal life fans out into every mode of movement and every habitat — an explosion of form that both scripture and biology find remarkable.

What science describes
  • 541 mya — Cambrian Explosion. Nearly all modern animal phyla appear in the fossil record within ~20 million years. Eyes, shells, jointed limbs, and predation arrive together.
  • 470 mya — plants colonise land, followed by arthropods.
  • 375 mya — lobe-finned fish such as Tiktaalik develop weight-bearing limbs; vertebrates walk.
  • 310 mya — the amniotic egg frees reptiles from water entirely.
  • 230 mya — dinosaurs radiate; mammals appear as small nocturnal insectivores.
  • 150 mya — Archaeopteryx; feathered dinosaurs take to the air.

Locomotion diversifies into a small number of recurring solutions: undulation on the belly, bipedal striding, quadrupedal gait, swimming, and powered flight — each evolving independently multiple times.

What scripture says
Qur'an

"Allah has created every moving creature from water. Of them are those that move on their bellies, of them are those that walk on two legs, and of them are those that walk on four."

Surah an-Nur 24:45
Qur'an

"And there is no creature on earth or bird that flies with its wings except that they are communities like you."

Surah al-Anʿam 6:38
Qur'an

"And there is no creature on earth but that upon Allah is its provision."

Surah Hud 11:6
Qur'an

"Do they not look at the birds above them, spreading and folding their wings? None holds them up except the Most Merciful."

Surah al-Mulk 67:19
Bible

"Let the earth bring forth the living creature after his kind, cattle, and creeping thing, and beast of the earth."

Genesis 1:24 (KJV)
Bible

"But ask now the beasts, and they shall teach thee; and the fowls of the air, and they shall tell thee."

Job 12:7 (KJV)
Bible

"O LORD, how manifold are thy works! in wisdom hast thou made them all."

Psalm 104:24 (KJV)
Reading them together: Qur'an 24:45 catalogues animal locomotion in precisely the categories a zoologist would use — belly, two legs, four — and grounds all of it in water, which is both the evolutionary origin and the chemical medium of life. Genesis 1:24 likewise has the earth bring forth the living creature, language that a number of Christian theologians from Augustine onward read as mediated rather than instantaneous production. Both texts also insist that animals are not mere resources: they are "communities like you," and they can teach.

Extinction and Renewal

443 – 66 million years ago · five global catastrophes

Five times, most of life is destroyed. Five times, what survives inherits an emptied world — including us.

What science describes
  • 443 mya — Ordovician–Silurian. Glaciation and sea-level fall; ~85% of species lost.
  • 374 mya — Late Devonian. Ocean anoxia; reef ecosystems collapse.
  • 252 mya — Permian–Triassic. "The Great Dying." Siberian Traps volcanism; ~96% of marine species lost. Life takes ~10 million years to recover.
  • 201 mya — Triassic–Jurassic. Clears the way for dinosaur dominance.
  • 66 mya — Cretaceous–Palaeogene. A ~10 km asteroid strikes Chicxulub, Yucatán. Impact winter follows. All non-avian dinosaurs vanish.

Mammals — small, burrowing, generalist — survive the K-Pg event and radiate into the vacated niches within ten million years. Primates appear shortly after. Without the asteroid, there is no plausible route to us.

What scripture says
Qur'an

"If He wills, He can do away with you and bring forth a new creation."

Surah Ibrahim 14:19; cf. Fatir 35:16
Qur'an

"And your Lord is the Free of need, the possessor of mercy. If He wills, He can do away with you and give succession after you to whomever He wills, just as He produced you from the descendants of another people."

Surah al-Anʿam 6:133
Qur'an

"We have decreed death among you… that We will change your likenesses and produce you in that [form] which you do not know. And you have already known the first creation, so will you not remember?"

Surah al-Waqiʿah 56:60–62
Bible

"Thou hidest thy face, they are troubled: thou takest away their breath, they die, and return to their dust."

Psalm 104:29 (KJV)
Bible

"All go unto one place; all are of the dust, and all turn to dust again."

Ecclesiastes 3:20 (KJV)
Reading them together: Qur'an 6:133 is striking in this context: succession is explicitly framed as replacement of one people by another, "just as He produced you from the descendants of another people" (dhurriyyati qawmin ākharīn). Whatever the verse's primary reference, the structure — one population giving way to a successor — is the structure of the fossil record. Both scriptures also refuse to treat destruction as the end of the story; extinction is a turning of the page, not the closing of the book.

The Hominin Line

7 million – 300,000 years ago

Apes stand upright, make tools, tame fire, and grow large brains. This is the epoch where science and theology most sharply require careful handling.

What science describes
  • 7 mya — the hominin line diverges from the chimpanzee lineage. Sahelanthropus.
  • 4.4–3.0 mya — Ardipithecus, then Australopithecus. "Lucy" (3.2 mya) walks upright. The Laetoli footprints preserve a bipedal gait in volcanic ash.
  • 2.6 mya — Oldowan stone tools. Homo habilis.
  • 1.9 mya — Homo erectus: modern body proportions, controlled fire, the first hominin to leave Africa.
  • 400 kya — Homo neanderthalensis in Europe and western Asia; Denisovans in the east.
  • 300 kya — anatomically modern Homo sapiens; earliest fossils at Jebel Irhoud, Morocco.

Cranial capacity roughly triples across this span. Genetics confirms interbreeding: most non-African humans today carry 1–2% Neanderthal DNA. Human beings are, on this account, one surviving twig of a formerly bushy family tree.

What scripture says
Qur'an

وَقَدْ خَلَقَكُمْ أَطْوَارًا

"…while He has created you in stages (aṭwāran)."

Surah Nuh 71:14
Qur'an

"You will surely embark upon stage after stage (ṭabaqan ʿan ṭabaq)."

Surah al-Inshiqaq 84:19
Qur'an

"…who perfected everything which He created and began the creation of man from clay."

Surah as-Sajdah 32:7
Qur'an

"And We did certainly create man out of clay from an altered black mud (ḥamaʾin masnūn)."

Surah al-Hijr 15:26
Hadith

"Allah created Adam from a handful which He took from all of the earth; so the children of Adam came in accordance with the earth — some red, some white, some black, and some in between."

Sunan Abi Dawud 4693; Jamiʿ at-Tirmidhi 2955 — graded hasan sahih
Bible

"And the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground."

Genesis 2:7 (KJV)
Bible

"…for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return."

Genesis 3:19 (KJV)
Reading them together: Both scriptures agree on one substantive claim that biology independently confirms: human beings are made of ordinary terrestrial matter. "Dust of the ground," "clay," "altered black mud" — the elemental composition of the human body is the elemental composition of the crust, and the Hadith of the handful taken from all the earth even ties human variation to the variation of the soil. Qur'anic language of aṭwār (stages) and ṭabaqan ʿan ṭabaq is read by some modern scholars as leaving room for developmental process; classical commentators applied it chiefly to embryology (nuṭfah → ʿalaqah → muḍghah, 23:12–14) and to the stages of a human life.
Where this gets genuinely contested. Whether Homo sapiens descends from earlier hominins, and how that squares with the direct creation of Adam, is not settled within either faith. Positions range from full rejection of common descent for humans, to acceptance of evolution for the body with a distinct divine act conferring the soul, to the view that Adam represents the first morally accountable human within an existing population. See Where Scholars Differ below. This page presents the range rather than adjudicating it.

The Threshold of Mind

300,000 – 50,000 years ago

Anatomically modern humans exist for a quarter of a million years — then something changes, and they begin to make art, bury their dead, and speak in symbols.

What science describes

Skeletons indistinguishable from ours appear by 300,000 years ago. But the archaeological signature of a fully modern mind arrives later and accumulates unevenly:

  • 100 kya — deliberate burial with grave goods; ochre processing at Blombos Cave.
  • 70 kya — engraved abstract patterns; shell beads worn as ornament.
  • 50–40 kya — the "Upper Palaeolithic transition": figurative cave art, bone flutes, standardised tools, long-distance trade.
  • 45 kya — humans cross open water to Australia; later, into the Americas.

The enabling capacities appear to be recursive symbolic language, which lets knowledge accumulate across generations rather than dying with the individual, and large-scale cooperation among unrelated strangers, achieved by no other species. Culture, not anatomy, becomes the dominant mode of human adaptation.

What scripture says
Qur'an

"The Most Merciful. Taught the Qur'an. Created man. Taught him eloquence (al-bayān)."

Surah ar-Rahman 55:1–4
Qur'an

"…Who taught by the pen — taught man that which he knew not."

Surah al-ʿAlaq 96:4–5 — the first revelation
Qur'an

"And of His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth and the diversity of your languages and your colours."

Surah ar-Rum 30:22
Hadith

"Every child is born upon the fiṭrah" — the innate disposition toward its Creator.

Sahih al-Bukhari 1358; Sahih Muslim 2658
Bible

"…he hath set the world in their heart."

Ecclesiastes 3:11 (KJV) — often rendered "eternity in their hearts"
Bible

"And out of the ground the LORD God formed every beast… and brought them unto Adam to see what he would call them."

Genesis 2:19 (KJV)
Reading them together: Both traditions single out naming and speech as the definitively human faculty — the Qur'an's al-bayān and teaching "by the pen," Genesis handing Adam the task of naming the animals. Archaeology arrives at the same place from the opposite direction: what separates the Upper Palaeolithic from everything before it is symbol. This convergence is conceptual rather than chronological, and it is the more interesting for that.

Adam Created: Clay, Proportion, and Breath

The theological moment · not a datable event

Here the two accounts part company in kind, not merely in detail. Scripture now describes something science has no instrument to detect: a creature shaped from the ground, given a breath that is not its own, and addressed by its Maker.

What science can and cannot say

On the material. The claim that a human being is made of earth is straightforwardly true. By mass the body is oxygen, carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, calcium and phosphorus — the same inventory, in different proportions, as the crust beneath it. Every atom was forged in a star, weathered into rock, dissolved into water, and taken up through food. There is no special human substance.

On subjugating other creatures. The archaeological record documents exactly the reordering scripture describes, and dates it. Dogs come under human direction by ~15,000 years ago; sheep and goats ~11,000; cattle and pigs ~10,500; horses ~5,500. Within a few millennia, one species is directing the reproduction, labour, and life-span of dozens of others, and reshaping whole landscapes to do it. No other animal has ever done this.

Where the instruments stop. Science can describe the neural substrate of what religion calls the soul — theory of mind, recursive language, autobiographical memory, moral emotion, the capacity to model one's own death. What it cannot do is adjudicate whether that substrate exhausts the phenomenon. Whether moral obligation genuinely binds, whether a person has standing before God — no experiment settles these. This is a boundary between kinds of question, not a gap awaiting better data.

What scripture says
Qur'an

"And We did certainly create man out of clay from an altered black mud (ḥamaʾin masnūn)."

Surah al-Hijr 15:26
Qur'an

"He created man from clay like pottery (ṣalṣālin ka'l-fakhkhār)."

Surah ar-Rahman 55:14 — the material is fired and hardened, not merely wet
Qur'an

فَإِذَا سَوَّيْتُهُ وَنَفَخْتُ فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِي فَقَعُوا لَهُ سَاجِدِينَ

"So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My spirit (rūḥī), then fall down to him in prostration."

Surah al-Hijr 15:29; Sad 38:72
Qur'an

"…who perfected everything which He created and began the creation of man from clay… then proportioned him and breathed into him from His spirit, and made for you hearing and vision and hearts."

Surah as-Sajdah 32:7–9 — the faculties are given with the breath
Qur'an

"Indeed, the example of Jesus with Allah is like that of Adam. He created him from dust; then He said to him, 'Be,' and he was."

Surah Al ʿImran 3:59
Hadith

"Allah created Adam from a handful which He took from all of the earth; so the children of Adam came in accordance with the earth — some red, some white, some black, and some in between."

Sunan Abi Dawud 4693; Tirmidhi 2955 — hasan sahih
Hadith

"The angels were created from light, the jinn from a smokeless flame of fire, and Adam from what has been described to you."

Sahih Muslim 2996 — three orders of creature, three materials
Qur'an

"And He has subjected to you (sakhkhara lakum) whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth — all from Him."

Surah al-Jathiyah 45:13; cf. 16:5–8, 36:71–73
Bible

"And the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul."

Genesis 2:7 (KJV)
Bible

"Thou madest him to have dominion over the works of thy hands; thou hast put all things under his feet."

Psalm 8:6 (KJV)
Reading them together: Both scriptures build the human being in two movements — an earthly material, then a divine breath — and both make the second movement the source of human standing. Note also that the Qur'an describes the clay through a progression of terms: turāb (dust), ṭīn (wet clay), ḥamaʾ masnūn (altered, aged mud), ṣalṣāl (dried, ringing clay). Whether that sequence is a description of process or a set of images for one act is exactly what the interpretive positions below divide over. The subjugation of other creatures (taskhīr) is not presented as conquest but as a delegation for which the delegate will answer.
A note on the sixty cubits. "Allah created Adam, and his height was sixty cubits" (Sahih al-Bukhari 3326; Muslim 2841) is authentic in transmission and creates real difficulty for a straightforward fit with the fossil record, which shows no hominin of ~27 metres. Responses vary: some take it literally as a miracle outside natural history; others read it of Adam's form in Paradise rather than on earth; others question the standard of the cubit. It is presented here unharmonised.

The Angels' Objection and the Refusal of Iblis

The announcement of the vicegerency

God announces a successor on earth. The angels raise a specific, evidence-shaped concern about bloodshed — and the question of how they knew to raise it opens onto everything that came before Adam.

The exchange, in sequence
1 · The announcement

"And when your Lord said to the angels, 'Indeed, I will make upon the earth a successive authority (khalīfah).'"

Surah al-Baqarah 2:30a
2 · The question

أَتَجْعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفْسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسْفِكُ الدِّمَاءَ

"They said, 'Will You place upon it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood, while we declare Your praise and sanctify You?' He said, 'Indeed, I know that which you do not know.'"

Surah al-Baqarah 2:30b
3 · The test

"And He taught Adam the names — all of them. Then He showed them to the angels and said, 'Inform Me of the names of these, if you are truthful.'"

Surah al-Baqarah 2:31
4 · The admission

"They said, 'Exalted are You; we have no knowledge except what You have taught us. Indeed, it is You who is the Knowing, the Wise.'"

Surah al-Baqarah 2:32
5 · The command

"And when We said to the angels, 'Prostrate before Adam,' they prostrated — except Iblis. He refused and was arrogant, and became of the disbelievers."

Surah al-Baqarah 2:34
6 · The refusal

"He said, 'I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay.'"

Surah al-Aʿraf 7:12; Sad 38:76
7 · Who he was

"…except Iblis. He was of the jinn and departed from the command of his Lord."

Surah al-Kahf 18:50 — he was never an angel
The bloodshed the angels named

The angels' concern was not vague. They specified two things: fasād, corruption of the earth, and safk al-dimāʾ, the shedding of blood. Both are documented in the human record from its earliest layers.

  • Jebel Sahaba, Sudan (~13,400 years ago) — a cemetery of some sixty individuals, many with projectile injuries and healed wounds from repeated attacks. The oldest known evidence of sustained intergroup violence.
  • Nataruk, Kenya (~10,000 years ago) — twenty-seven individuals killed together, several bound, including women and children. A massacre among hunter-gatherers, before cities or states existed.
  • Talheim, Germany (~7,000 years ago) — an entire early farming community killed with adzes and buried in a pit.

And the corruption is measurable too: the megafaunal extinctions that follow human arrival on every continent and island, from the mammoth and the moa to the thylacine; deforestation; and, in our own century, a rate of species loss that geologists now debate naming as an extinction event in its own right.

Whatever one concludes about the metaphysics, the angels' empirical prediction has an unambiguous verdict in the ground.

Why did the angels say it? This is the question the passage forces, because the angels appear to know something they had not been told. The Qur'an does not answer it directly, and the exegetical tradition offers four explanations, which are not mutually exclusive:
  • They had seen it before. The most widely transmitted view. Al-Ṭabarī, al-Qurṭubī and Ibn Kathīr record reports attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Masʿūd and others that the earth was inhabited before Adam — by the jinn — who spread corruption and shed blood there, until an angelic host was sent against them. The angels therefore reasoned by analogy from creatures they had watched fill the earth with violence: another earth-dweller, they inferred, would do the same.
  • They read it. Some held that the angels had seen the matter written in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawḥ al-Maḥfūẓ).
  • The word itself told them. A khalīfah is one who arbitrates and settles disputes — which presupposes that there will be disputes to settle. The inference is contained in the announcement.
  • They inferred it from the material. Al-Rāzī notes the view that a creature compounded of earth, with appetite and need, will necessarily compete — unlike beings of light, who neither hunger nor inherit.
What the exchange actually establishes. Three things, each of which the following epochs depend on:
  • The angels were not protesting. The overwhelming majority of commentators read their words as istifhām istikshāf — a request to understand the wisdom, not an objection to the decree. God's reply, "I know that which you do not know," does not deny their prediction. It concedes the bloodshed and points past it: to the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the saints who would also come from this creature.
  • The test was of knowledge, not of purity. Adam's qualification is not that he is better behaved than the angels — he is not — but that he can be taught the names. Superiority here is the capacity to know, to categorise, to speak. That is precisely the faculty archaeology identifies as the hinge of human history.
  • Iblis's error was to reason from substance. He was not an angel but of the jinn (18:50), which is why he could disobey. His argument — fire outranks clay — is a piece of analogical reasoning set against an explicit command, and it ignores the one thing that mattered: what had been breathed into the clay. Classical scholars treat this as the first instance of arrogance (kibr), and as a warning about reasoning that weighs materials while overlooking the divine act.
The Biblical parallels
Bible

"And it came to pass… that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him."

Genesis 4:8 (KJV) — bloodshed arrives in the first generation
Bible

"…let all the angels of God worship him."

Hebrews 1:6 (KJV) — angelic homage, though directed to the Son
Bible

"How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning!"

Isaiah 14:12 (KJV) — traditionally read of the adversary's fall through pride
Bible

"I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven."

Luke 10:18 (KJV)
The angels vindicated
Hadith

"No soul is killed unjustly but a share of its sin falls upon the first son of Adam, for he was the first to establish killing."

Sahih al-Bukhari 3335; Sahih Muslim 1677
Qur'an

"Corruption has appeared throughout the land and sea by what the hands of people have earned."

Surah ar-Rum 30:41
Qur'an

"…whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption in the land — it is as if he had slain mankind entirely."

Surah al-Ma'idah 5:32
Qur'an

"Then We made you successors in the land after them, that We may observe how you will do."

Surah Yunus 10:14 — the vicegerency is an examination
On the pre-Adamic reports. The narrations describing jinn on earth before Adam are āthār — statements of Companions and Successors recorded in the tafsir literature — not marfūʿ hadith traced to the Prophet, and several show the influence of earlier Near Eastern material (isrāʾīliyyāt). They are widely transmitted and widely cited, but they carry less authority than Qur'an or Sahih hadith, and scholars have long differed over how much weight to give them. Some contemporary writers extend them to read the angels' knowledge as drawn from watching pre-Adamic hominins fill the earth with violence. That extension is a modern proposal, not a classical position, and it is offered here as one reading among several rather than as established interpretation.

The Six Days, Read Carefully

Qur'an 7:54, 10:3, 11:7, 25:59, 32:4, 50:38, 57:4 · Genesis 1

Both scriptures say six. Neither says what a day is, and the Qur'an says elsewhere that a divine day may be a thousand years or fifty thousand. What follows is what each text actually states, and where the honest limits of correlation lie.

Before the table

The strongest claim defensible here is compatibility, not confirmation. Where a verse and a finding sit comfortably together, that is worth noting. Where a correlation only works by straining the Arabic, this page says so rather than reaching.

The Genesis and Qur'anic sequences are not the same, and the table below shows where they part. That difference is old, well documented, and not resolved by either tradition.

The word itself

Yawm in Arabic means a day, but also a period, an epoch, an age. The Qur'an uses it for the 24-hour day, for the Day of Judgement, and for spans it explicitly measures in thousands of years.

Qur'an

وَإِنَّ يَوْمًا عِندَ رَبِّكَ كَأَلْفِ سَنَةٍ مِّمَّا تَعُدُّونَ

"And indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of those which you count."

Surah al-Hajj 22:47
Qur'an

"The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him during a Day the measure of which is fifty thousand years."

Surah al-Maʿarij 70:4

The consequence. Two verses give two different lengths for a divine day. Classical commentators drew the obvious conclusion: these are not arithmetic. Yawm denotes a stage, and its duration is not something the text is telling us.

What the tradition already said

Ibn Kathir records the disagreement plainly: some early authorities held the six days to be days as we know them; others held each to be a thousand years. He does not resolve it.

Al-Tabari preserves both readings side by side, which is his usual practice when the tradition genuinely divided.

Augustine, writing around 400 CE in De Genesi ad Litteram, argued the Genesis days could not be ordinary days — since the sun is not made until the fourth. His reasoning is textual, not scientific, and it predates geology by fourteen centuries.

Worth being clear about. Non-literal readings of the six days are not a modern retreat in the face of science. They are attested in both traditions long before anyone knew the Earth's age.

The sequence in the Qur'an

The Qur'an nowhere gives a numbered day-by-day list. What it gives is a sequence, spread across several passages — most fully in Surah Fussilat 41:9–12.

Stage 1— two days

خَلَقَ الْأَرْضَ فِي يَوْمَيْنِ

"He created the earth in two days." 41:9

Accretion of the proto-Earth from the solar nebula, roughly 4.6 to 4.5 billion years ago. Radiometric dating of meteorites gives 4.567 billion years, consistent across several independent isotope systems.

Stage 2— two days

وَجَعَلَ فِيهَا رَوَاسِيَ مِن فَوْقِهَا وَبَارَكَ فِيهَا وَقَدَّرَ فِيهَا أَقْوَاتَهَا

"And He placed on it firmly set mountains above it, and blessed it, and determined therein its sustenance — in four days." 41:10

Crust formation, orogeny, the arrival of water, and the conditions that make sustenance possible. The oldest known continental crust — the Acasta gneiss — dates to about 4.03 billion years.

A translation point that matters. The verse says four days, and most scholars read this as four days in total including the two of the previous verse — not four more. Otherwise the sum exceeds six. The Arabic supports the inclusive reading; several English translations obscure it.

Stage 3— two days

فَقَضَاهُنَّ سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ فِي يَوْمَيْنِ

"And He completed them as seven heavens in two days, and inspired in each heaven its command." 41:12

The passage places this after the earth's preparation. Cosmologically the heavens long precede the Earth, which is a real ordering difficulty, addressed below rather than smoothed over.

The ordering problem, stated honestly. Read plainly, Fussilat puts the earth first and the heavens after. Cosmology puts the universe at 13.8 billion years and the Earth at 4.6. Three responses exist in the literature: that thumma in 41:11 marks a shift of subject rather than a step in time; that Surah al-Naziʿat 79:27–30 gives the reverse order and the two passages describe different aspects rather than a single chronology; or that the passages are not making a chronological claim at all. None of these is universally accepted, and anyone who tells you the matter is settled is overstating it.

The sequence in Genesis

Day 1

Light, and its separation from darkness. Genesis 1:3–5

Day 2

The firmament, dividing the waters above from those below. 1:6–8

Day 3

Dry land, seas, and vegetation. 1:9–13

Day 4

Sun, moon and stars, for signs and seasons. 1:14–19

Day 5

Sea creatures and birds. 1:20–23

Day 6

Land animals, and humankind in God's image. 1:24–31

The two accounts are not the same account. Genesis makes light on day one and the sun on day four. It puts vegetation before the sun that vegetation requires. It gives birds before land animals; the fossil record gives the reverse by a wide margin. These are not difficulties invented by critics — they were noticed within the tradition, and they are why Augustine reached for a non-literal reading in the fifth century.
Point Genesis Qur'an Where science sits
Number of stages Six, numbered explicitly Six, stated but not enumerated Not a scientific question
Length of a stage Unstated; "evening and morning" implies a day Unstated; 22:47 and 70:4 give 1,000 and 50,000 years 13.8 billion years total; 4.6 for Earth
Rest afterwards God rests on the seventh day (2:2) Explicitly denied — "no weariness touched Us" (50:38) —
Order of sun and plants Plants day 3, sun day 4 No such sequence given Sun precedes all life by billions of years
Heavens and earth Heavens and earth together at the start Ordering differs between 41:9–12 and 79:27–30 Universe long precedes Earth
Origin of humans Formed from dust, day six From clay, in stages; no day specified Common descent; ~300,000 years for H. sapiens

How readers have handled this

Literal six days

The days are ordinary days and the Earth is young. Held by a minority in both traditions. Its strength is that it takes the plain sense seriously; its difficulty is that it must reject radiometric dating, cosmology and geology together, not one at a time.

Day-age

Each day is a long epoch. Fits yawm's range and 22:47 comfortably, and has classical precedent. Its difficulty is the ordering — day-age does not rescue vegetation before the sun.

Framework or literary

The six days are a structure for teaching rather than a chronology — Genesis pairs days 1–3 (forming realms) with days 4–6 (filling them), which is a literary pattern rather than a timeline. Explains the ordering elegantly. Critics say it concedes too much of the text's own voice.

Non-concordist

The texts address why and by whom, science addresses how and when, and correlating them is a category error that flatters neither. Held by many working scientists of faith. Its cost is that it gives up the apologetic appeal of correspondence entirely.

What can be said without overstating. That both traditions describe creation as staged rather than instantaneous is genuinely notable, and it sits comfortably beside a universe with a history. That is a modest claim, and it is defensible. The stronger claim — that these verses encode modern cosmology — requires reading the Arabic and the Hebrew more tightly than either language permits, and it tends not to survive contact with a specialist in the language. The modest claim is the one worth making.

The Trust, the Fall, and the Descent

The moral beginning of history

Freedom is granted, misused, and — in one tradition decisively, in the other partially — repaired. Here Islam and Christianity diverge most instructively.

The Qur'anic account
Qur'an

"Indeed, We offered the Trust (amānah) to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, and they declined to bear it and feared it; but man undertook it. Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant."

Surah al-Ahzab 33:72
Qur'an

"O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in Paradise and eat from wherever you will but do not approach this tree."

Surah al-Aʿraf 7:19
Qur'an

"…and Adam disobeyed his Lord and erred. Then his Lord chose him, and turned to him in forgiveness, and guided him."

Surah Ta-Ha 20:121–122
Qur'an

"Then Adam received from his Lord words, and He accepted his repentance."

Surah al-Baqarah 2:37
Qur'an

"And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another."

Surah al-Anʿam 6:164 — no inherited guilt
The Biblical account
Bible

"Of every tree of the garden thou mayest freely eat: but of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it."

Genesis 2:16–17 (KJV)
Bible

"…and she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat."

Genesis 3:6 (KJV)
Bible

"Therefore the LORD God sent him forth from the garden of Eden, to till the ground."

Genesis 3:23 (KJV)
Bible

"Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin…"

Romans 5:12 (KJV) — the basis of original sin
Bible

"And have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air."

Genesis 1:28 (KJV) — dominion as stewardship
Reading them together: The narratives run in close parallel — a garden, a prohibition, a tempter, a transgression, an expulsion — and then diverge sharply on consequence. In the Qur'an, Adam repents and is forgiven before the descent; his fall is a lapse, not a corruption of nature, and 6:164 explicitly rules out inherited guilt. In Pauline Christianity, the fall transmits a condition that requires redemption, which is why 1 Corinthians frames Christ as the "last Adam." The Qur'an also assigns the transgression to both together rather than to Eve, and names no serpent — Iblis speaks directly. These are not variant tellings of one story so much as two theologies of the human condition using shared imagery.

The Two Creation Accounts, Side by Side

Genesis and the Qur’an describe the same event differently — the order of the days, the rest on the seventh, and the making of Adam all diverge. Set out plainly rather than harmonised.

Where Genesis 1 and the Qur'anic material describe the same sequence, and where they differ:

Element Genesis / Bible Qur'an & Hadith Point of difference
Duration Six days, then rest on the seventh (Gen 1:31–2:2) Six ayyām / periods (7:54, 41:9–12); no rest — "no fatigue touched Us" (50:38) The Qur'an explicitly denies divine rest, reading it as implying limitation.
Order Light → firmament → land & plants → luminaries → sea life & birds → land animals & man Earth in two periods → provisions in four → heavens in two (41:9–12) Genesis gives a strict day-by-day sequence; the Qur'an is thematic and dispersed.
Method "And God said, Let there be…" — creation by word "Kun fayakūn" — "Be, and it is" (2:117, 36:82) Substantially the same: creation by command, not by struggle against chaos.
Human material "Dust of the ground" (Gen 2:7) Turāb (dust, 3:59), ṭīn (clay, 32:7), ḥamaʾ masnūn (altered mud, 15:26), ṣalṣāl (sounding clay, 55:14) The Qur'an gives a graded sequence of materials; Genesis gives one term.
The divine breath "Breathed into his nostrils the breath of life" (Gen 2:7) "Breathed into him of My spirit" (15:29, 32:9) Closely parallel; Islam avoids the "image and likeness" language of Gen 1:26.
Creation of Eve From Adam's rib during sleep (Gen 2:21–22) "From it He created its mate" (4:1, 39:6); rib appears in Hadith (Bukhari 3331) rather than Qur'an The Qur'anic text is not explicit about the rib; the Hadith is often read figuratively.
The tempter The serpent (Gen 3:1) Iblis / Shayṭān, addressing them directly (7:20, 20:120) No serpent in the Qur'anic account.

Where Scholars Differ

There is no single religious position on human origins. Several serious ones exist within both Islam and Christianity, and each is given with what it costs to hold.

There is no single religious position on human origins, and presenting one as consensus would be dishonest. Within Islam and Christianity alike, serious scholars occupy several positions, each with its own textual reasoning and its own difficulties. The four below cover most of the field.

1. Special creation, no common descent

Adam was created directly and miraculously, with no biological ancestry. Fossil hominins are either separate creations or misinterpreted. Strength: takes the texts at face value, including the sixty-cubit Hadith. Difficulty: requires rejecting a very large and mutually corroborating body of genetic and palaeontological evidence.

2. Evolution of the body, special creation of the soul

Biological evolution proceeded as described, but at a chosen point God conferred the rūḥ — moral and spiritual accountability — on a member of the lineage. Strength: preserves both the science and the theological uniqueness of the human person. Difficulty: must reinterpret the clay narratives as symbolic. This is broadly the position of Catholic teaching since Humani Generis (1950).

3. Adam as first accountable human within a population

Adam is historical but not the sole biological ancestor — the first to receive revelation and moral responsibility within an existing human population. Strength: compatible with population genetics, which finds no bottleneck of two. Difficulty: strains verses describing all humanity as "children of Adam."

4. Non-concordism

Scripture and science answer different questions and should not be harmonised at all. The creation narratives are theological and liturgical texts about meaning, purpose, and covenant — not about mechanism. Strength: avoids forcing either discipline. Difficulty: some find it concedes too much historical content.

On concordism generally. The practice of matching scriptural verses to current scientific findings — sometimes called iʿjāz ʿilmī or "scientific miracle" literature — has been criticised from within the religious traditions themselves, notably by scholars who point out that science revises itself. A verse harmonised with the physics of one generation may need re-harmonising with the next, which makes faith hostage to the current state of a discipline. Classical exegesis, working centuries before modern science, read most of these verses quite differently. Readers are encouraged to hold the correspondences on this page lightly, as invitations to reflection rather than as proofs.

Conclusion: Two Books, One Reality

What can honestly be claimed after all of it — and the difference between compatibility, which is defensible, and confirmation, which is not.

The medieval formulation was that God wrote two books — the book of scripture and the book of nature — and that they cannot finally contradict, since the author is one. That framing, common to Ibn Rushd, Maimonides, and Aquinas alike, does not resolve every tension. It does, however, set the right expectation: that apparent conflict signals a misreading of one book or the other, and that the honest response is more careful reading rather than louder assertion.

Across thirteen and a half billion years, the scientific account is one of increasing complexity emerging from simple rules — nuclei from quarks, atoms from nuclei, stars from atoms, chemistry from stars, life from chemistry, mind from life. It is a magnificent account, and it is incomplete in a specific way: it describes the trajectory without adjudicating whether the trajectory means anything. That question is not a gap in the data. It is a different kind of question.

What scripture adds is not an alternative mechanism but a claim about standing. The khalīfah is entrusted; the one made in the image is addressed; and both are answerable. Whether the reader finds that claim true is beyond what any timeline can settle. But it is worth noticing that the faculty scripture identifies as decisive — the capacity to name, to know, to be spoken to — is the same faculty that archaeology identifies as the point where our species began to leave a record at all.

"Are those who know equal to those who do not know?" — Qur'an 39:9. The question is rhetorical, and it is addressed to anyone who reads either book carefully.

From Mathematics to Engineering and Innovation

Pillar One: Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics

STEM: How We Found Out

"What I cannot create, I do not understand." — Richard Feynman, on his blackboard at his death, 1988

Science is not a list of facts. It is a method for being wrong in public, carefully, until what survives is worth trusting. This page walks the six disciplines that method built — mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology, engineering, and the study of mind and machine — and asks of each: what is the one idea that reorganises everything else?

How to read this page

Each discipline gets a short section built the same way. A one-line core idea, then a side-by-side panel: what the field claims on the left, where it runs out on the right. Beneath that, expandable cards for the detail — open only what you want.

Nothing here needs prior study. Equations appear only where a sentence would be longer than the formula. The last two sections — misconceptions and the timeline — are the ones most worth reading if you are short of time.
